subject: Post-demo integration qualification & SDK environment prerequisites
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@lumina.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: integration questions & next steps

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team at Lumina is excited about Redwood's latency/cost claims. We had a few technical follow-ups from engineering that I'd like to capture so we can scope a short POC. High-level asks: 

- SDK quickstart: Python + TypeScript samples for local mocking and a simple serverless deploy
- Auth: what's the recommended auth for hosted vs private (API key, OAuth, mTLS)? Any short-lived token examples?
- Routing & structured output: we need to support tool-calling style responses and deterministic JSON schema enforcement for downstream processors
- Embeddings & reranking: are there recommended quantized model options and an example reranker pipeline?

Can you confirm whether Redwood provides a smoke-test script we can run locally and any environment variable checklist? Also, our infra doc is attached (lumina-infra-notes.pdf) — it includes current throughput targets (we're targeting ~500 qps initially, spike to 1.5k qps).

Next steps from our side: schedule technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your SDK engineer and ours. We can be flexible this week.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Patel
CTO, Lumina
sam@lumina.ai

Attachment: lumina-infra-notes.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@lumina.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: integration questions & next steps

Sam — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the infra doc. Quick recap and proposed plan: 

1) SDK quickstart + local smoke tests (deliverable by Redwood):
   - We’ll send a ZIP with Python and TypeScript sample apps (minimal server + client) and an env-smoke-test.sh that verifies connectivity, auth, and a simple generation request.
   - Included checklist: required env vars (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, REDWOOD_REGION, LOG_LEVEL).

2) Auth recommendations:
   - Hosted: API key with short-lived session tokens via our token exchange (sample included).
   - Private/VPC: optional mTLS or API key + KMS-managed key wrapping; we’ll include both examples.

3) Routing & structured output:
   - We’ll include a TypeScript example for function/tool calling and a validation layer that enforces a JSON schema on the model output (soft and hard enforcement patterns).

4) Embeddings & reranker:
   - Recommendation: start with our medium-cost embedding model for retrieval; reranking via a small cross-encoder on a dedicated instance. Provide a sample reranker scaffold and perf knobs.

5) Next steps / scheduling:
   - Technical deep-dive w/Dev on Thu 6/18 10:00–10:45 PT (proposed). Please confirm attendee list and desired agenda items.
   - I attached a short checklist (redwood-sdk-setup-checklist.pdf) — run that before the call if you can.

If that aligns, Aisha will coordinate the calendar invite and I’ll drop the sample bundle into the Drive link below.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-sdk-setup-checklist.pdf (PDF, 45KB)
Related link: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/quickstart-sdk-samples

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: integration questions & next steps — tech notes

Adding a few technical notes that we should surface in the deep-dive and include in the sample apps: 

- Local testing approach:
  * Python: lightweight FastAPI sample that wraps the Redwood SDK call, with a docker-compose file for local env and a small script (env-smoke-test.sh) to validate request/response.
  * TypeScript: Node + Express sample and a Vite-based front-end sample to demo streaming + tool-calling.

- Env & secrets:
  * Use REDWOOD_API_KEY for quickstarts; sample token-exchange flow will demonstrate how to mint short-lived keys for browser clients.
  * For Private customers, include mTLS cert generation doc + example systemd unit that runs the runtime behind TLS.

- Routing & performance knobs:
  * Show policy example: route to model-tier "cost-optimized" for background reranking, and "latency-optimized" for interactive chat.
  * Include a snippet that toggles continuous batching and KV cache TTL for sessions.

- Structured output/tool-calling:
  * Provide a TypeScript helper to declare functions and validation schema; include example of fallback to a parser when strict validation fails.

- Embeddings + reranker sample:
  * Provide a small pipeline: embedding index (FAISS) -> retrieval -> lightweight cross-encoder rerank (pseudocode + perf targets).

Attachments for demo: env-smoke-test.sh (bash), a small README explaining how to run the local demo, and the sample-apps zip. I’ll prepare the code snippets and push to the Drive ahead of the call.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: env-smoke-test.sh, sample-apps.zip

From: Sam Patel <sam@lumina.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-team@lumina.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: integration questions & next steps

Hannah / team — this is great, thanks. Quick answers from our infra side after a short review of your checklist and our internal doc: 

- We’ll start with hosted to speed the POC. API key flow is fine for now; we’ll evaluate mTLS for a later private deployment.
- Throughput: start at 500 qps with a steady-state target of 1.5k qps over a month. Latency SLO for interactive paths is 150–250ms p99.
- Embeddings + rerank: yes, we want embeddings for retrieval followed by a reranker. Perf is important — we’ll measure end-to-end latency and cost per query.
- Attendees for Thu 6/18 deep-dive: Sam Patel (CTO), Maya R. (eng lead) — the eng alias will include two backend engineers.

I confirmed the call time and we’ll run your smoke test before the meeting. I attached an updated infra notes pdf. Looking forward to the sample bundle.

Best,
Sam
Sam Patel
CTO, Lumina
sam@lumina.ai

Attachment: lumina-infra-notes.pdf (updated)
